trust_decision.summary: Whether a requestor may use a task ID is decided per request in the four auto-registered default task handlers of the low-level server, by comparing the session scope embedded in the requested task ID with the scope assigned to the requestor's session when the session was configured for task support (unscoped IDs are allowed for get/result/cancel, and are never listed).

landing_point.why: The advisory says the default task handlers let any client access and cancel other clients' tasks; `_register_default_task_handlers` is exactly the code that `server.experimental.enable_tasks()` installs for tasks/get, tasks/result, tasks/list and tasks/cancel (docs/experimental/tasks-server.md:50-54), and none of the four handlers consults the requesting session.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: A task ID the caller chose explicitly is the caller's own capability and is only deprecated, not unsupported, and a stateless server has no stable session to bind a task to - so a solver can argue the session-configuration layer (configure_session / Server.run stateless plumbing) is out of scope and leave unscoped IDs open to any requestor.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Explicitly chosen task IDs (singleton/named jobs) and tasks created in stateless mode must stay reachable by any session that presents the exact ID, and tasks created directly through a TaskStore must stay readable by ID; an over-broad fix that binds every task to its creator (or makes run_task reject an explicit task_id) breaks these, and the pinned suite even asserts store-created tasks are listed (tests/experimental/tasks/server/test_server.py:506-515), so a strict list filter turns an existing green test red.

O6_input_shapes: task ID generated by run_task: 32 hex chars of session scope, ':', canonical uuid4
task ID with no scope: caller-supplied task_id, ID minted by TaskStore.create_task, and any ID on a stateless session
near-miss IDs that must NOT be treated as scoped: uppercase hex scope, scope half of the wrong length, non-uuid4 suffix, bare uuid4, empty string, trailing newline
tasks/list with params present and absent (cursor supplied / not supplied) and a store listing longer than one page
requestor session whose scope is None (stateless or task support not configured): get/result/cancel deny scoped IDs, list returns nothing

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Give TaskResultHandler.handle() an optional session_scope argument and enforce the scope inside it, so tasks/result is protected for every caller instead of only the default handler.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: handle() is the one shared control point for tasks/result and already receives the requesting session; the fix's own docstring pushes the decision onto whoever calls it, so a maintainer wanting defence in depth would move the check inside.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: cancel_task(store, task_id, session_scope=...) rejecting a task whose embedded scope is another session's.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The helper is the documented building block for custom handlers (its docstring shows @server.experimental.cancel_task()), so scoping it there closes every custom cancel route at once.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Apply the scope check inside the get_task/get_task_result/list_tasks/cancel_task decorator wrappers, so app-registered custom handlers are scoped by default with an explicit opt-out.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: enable_tasks() only guards its own default handlers; an app that registers a custom handler re-opens the hole, which is the natural follow-up a maintainer would write for a 'secure by default' release.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Attach the creating session to the task with an ad-hoc per-handler task_id->session dict (or a field on Task) and guard only tasks/get and tasks/cancel, leaving tasks/result and tasks/list - including its pagination cursor - unfiltered.

out_of_scope_notes: Adjacent but outside this advisory's task-access property: TaskResultHandler keeps one _pending_requests dict for all sessions (src/mcp/server/experimental/task_result_handler.py:201-235), so a queued elicitation/sampling response arriving on one session could resolve another session's pending request id; not pursued.
